arxiv-1802-08876.title: Lovász Meets Weisfeiler and Leman
arxiv-1802-08876.creator: Holger Dell, Martin Grohe, Gaurav Rattan
arxiv-1802-08876.description: A 2018 arXiv research paper by Holger Dell, Martin Grohe, Gaurav Rattan. In this paper, we relate a beautiful theory by Lovász with a popular heuristic algorithm for the graph isomorphism problem, namely the color refinement algorithm and its k k -dimensional generalization known as the Weisfeiler-Leman algorithm.

arxiv-1908-11118.title: Determining Surface Phase Diagrams Including Anharmonic Effects
arxiv-1908-11118.creator: Yuanyuan Zhou, Matthias Scheffler, Luca M. Ghiringhelli
arxiv-1908-11118.description: Abstract We introduce a massively parallel replica-exchange grand-canonical sampling algorithm to simulate materials at realistic conditions, in particular surfaces and clusters in reactive atmospheres. Its purpose is to determine in an automated fashion equilibrium phase diagrams for a given potential-energy surface (PES) and for any observable sampled in the grand-canonical ensemble.

arxiv-2412-05125.title: Optimal control under uncertainty with joint chance state constraints: almost-everywhere bounds, variance reduction, and application to (bi-)linear elliptic PDEs Thanks: Version from August 24, 2026.
arxiv-2412-05125.creator: Rene Henrion, Georg Stadler, Florian Wechsung
arxiv-2412-05125.description: Abstract We study optimal control of PDEs under uncertainty with the state variable subject to joint chance constraints. The controls are deterministic, but the states are probabilistic due to random variables in the governing equation. Joint chance constraints ensure that the random state variable meets pointwise bounds with high probability.

arxiv-2509-15543.title: Nonconvex Decentralized Stochastic Bilevel Optimization under Heavy-Tailed Noises
arxiv-2509-15543.creator: Xinwen Zhang, Yihan Zhang, Hongchang Gao
arxiv-2509-15543.description: Abstract Existing decentralized stochastic optimization methods assume the lower-level loss function is strongly convex and the stochastic gradient noise has finite variance. These strong assumptions typically are not satisfied in real-world machine learning models. To address these limitations, we develop a novel decentralized stochastic bilevel optimization algorithm for the nonconvex bilevel optimization problem under heavy-tailed noises.

pmc-11430486.title: Overcoming Antigen Escape and T-Cell Exhaustion in CAR-T Therapy for Leukemia
pmc-11430486.creator: Elżbieta Bartoszewska, Maciej Tota, Monika Kisielewska, Izabela Skowron, Kamil Sebastianka, Oliwia Stefaniak, Klaudia Molik, Jakub Rubin, Karolina Kraska, Anna Choromańska, João T Barata
pmc-11430486.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Leukemia is a prevalent pediatric cancer with significant challenges, particularly in relapsed or refractory cases. Chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR-T) therapy has emerged as a personalized cancer treatment, modifying patients’ T cells to target and destroy resistant cancer cells. This study reviews the current therapeutic options of CAR-T therapy for leukemia, addressing the primary obstacles such as antigen escape and T-cell exhaustion. We explore dual-targeting strategies and their potential to improve treatment outcomes by preventing the loss of target antigens.

pmc-12738691.title: Generation and ophthalmological characterization of oculocutaneous albinism type 1 pig models by selection-free genome editing
pmc-12738691.creator: Dongjin Oh, Cheong Seok, Hyun Woo Park, Soomin Park, Joohyeong Lee, Hyerin Choi, Ali Jawad, Jaehyung Ham, Hyewon Jang, Sang Chul Lee, Byoung Chol Oh, Changjong Moon, Kyung Ho Park, Sang-Hwan Hyun, Daesik Kim
pmc-12738691.description: Oculocutaneous albinism type 1 (OCA1) is an autosomal recessive disorder caused by mutations in the tyrosinase (TYR) gene, resulting in melanin deficiency and severe visual impairments. Although mouse models provide insights into OCA1 pathogenesis, they exhibit significant anatomical and physiological differences from humans, particularly in ocular structure and function, thereby limiting their ability to recapitulate human OCA1 phenotypes.

pmc-13090631.title: Protocol for deriving proliferating primary fibroblast cultures from Malabar red snapper larvae for cytogenetic analysis
pmc-13090631.creator: Kathiresan Purushothaman, Muhammad Hazim bin Mohamed, Saraphina Dianne Tneo Rwei Qing, Nguyen Thanh Vu, Bing Liang, Harmeet Singh, Tan Shixiong, Grace Loo, Saraswathy Bisa, Dean R. Jerry, Jose A. Domingos, Shubha Vij
pmc-13090631.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). SummaryHere, we present a protocol for deriving primary fibroblast cultures from early-stage Malabar red snapper (Lutjanus malabaricus) larvae for cytogenetic analysis. We describe steps for dissociating larval tissues using trypsin and culturing them to establish proliferating fibroblast cells. We then detail procedures for arresting cells at metaphase by colchicine treatment, followed by hypotonic treatment, methanol-acetic acid fixation, and Giemsa staining to visualize chromosomes. This protocol yields clear metaphase spreads suitable for karyotype analysis and downstream cytogenetic applications.

uslaw-usc-t10-s8862.title: 10 U.S.C. § 8862 — Duties of marshal
uslaw-usc-t10-s8862.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t10-s8862.description: United States Code, Title 10 (Armed Forces); Part IV (General Administration); Chapter 883 (Prize). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. The marshal shall— (1) keep in his custody all persons found on board a prize and sent in as witnesses, until they are released by the prize commissioners or the court; (2) keep safely in his custody all prize property under warrant from.
